MALACAÑAN PALACE
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES
[ EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 561, February 02, 1953 ]
ORGANIZING A CERTAIN PORTION OF THE MUNICIPALITY OF CANTILAN, PROVINCE OF
SURIGAO, INTO AN INDEPENDENT MUNICIPALITY UNDER THE NAME OF MADRID.
Upon the recommendation of the Provincial Board of Surigao and pursuant to the provisions of section 68 of
the Revised Administrative Code, there is hereby organized in the Province of Surigao a municipality to be
known as the municipality of Madrid which shall consist of the eastern part of the municipality of Cantilan
and more particularly bounded and described by the following boundary lines:
Beginning from a point in Cantilan River near the sea immediately west of the poblacion of the barrio of
Union, running southerly in a straight imaginary line to kilometer 126 in the sitio of Tagcoling along the
national road; thence southeasterly straight to a point where it first coincides with the lower course of the
Sibyoc River somewhere west of the sitio of Labao; thence, following the course of the Sibyoc River
upstream until it intersects the Surigao-Agusan boundary in the Diwata Mountains; thence, following the
Surigao-Agusan boundary in a northeasterly direction until it reaches the point where the Cantilan-Lanuza
boundary meets the Surigao-Agusan boundary; thence, following the Cantilan-Lanuza boundary until it
touches the seashore; and thence following the limits of the marine waters which the municipality of Madrid
shall have pursuant to section 2321 of the Revised Administrative Code to the point of beginning. (Reference
used: Map of the municipality of Cantilan, showing the proposed municipality of Madrid, etc., scale
1:125,000 prepared by Surveyman C A. Cuison, approved and submitted by District Engineer Galo C.
Castronuevo.)
